approaches.name: Learn From The Data Itself
approaches.problem: Most useful data does not arrive with hand-written answers, but it still has repeated structure.
approaches.how_it_works: Create a training task from the example rather than from a human label. Hide part of the input, predict a neighboring part, reconstruct a compressed version, assign likelihood to the full example, or generate a related sample. The model improves only when it discovers repeatable structure that helps solve that self-made task.
approaches.why_it_matters: This turns large unlabeled collections into training signal instead of waiting for expensive human labels.
approaches.failure_mode: The model can learn shortcuts that solve the training task without learning structure that helps later.

approaches.name: Separate Modeling Goals
approaches.problem: A method can be good at likelihood, samples, compression, or features, and those are not the same goal.
approaches.how_it_works: Sort each method by the object it learns and the evidence it uses. Likelihood models learn p(x), latent models learn hidden z and p(x|z), GANs learn a generator judged by a discriminator, diffusion models learn denoising directions, and self-supervised models learn representations for later transfer. Then judge each method by the goal it was built for.
approaches.why_it_matters: It prevents comparing models by one score when they were built to solve different pressures.
approaches.failure_mode: A method can look strong under one goal while being weak for the actual use case.

approaches.name: Chain-Rule Likelihood
approaches.problem: The full probability of a high-dimensional object is hard to model directly.
approaches.how_it_works: Choose an order for the components of x, then write the full probability as a product of conditional probabilities. Train one conditional predictor for every position using the true previous components as context. The full log likelihood becomes a sum of next-piece log probabilities, so training is ordinary cross-entropy or negative log likelihood across positions.
approaches.why_it_matters: Training and scoring become exact because each conditional probability is a normal supervised prediction problem.
approaches.failure_mode: Generation is slow and early sampled mistakes become part of the context for later predictions.

approaches.name: Teacher-Forced Training
approaches.problem: During training the model needs clean context, but during generation it must use its own past outputs.
approaches.how_it_works: During training, feed the true prefix from the dataset into the model at every position, even if the model would have sampled something else. This lets all positions produce supervised losses in parallel. During generation, switch to feeding back the model’s own sampled outputs, one step at a time, until the sequence is complete.
approaches.why_it_matters: This makes large sequence models train efficiently on every position of every example.
approaches.failure_mode: The model can be surprised by its own imperfect samples because training context was cleaner than sampling context.

approaches.name: Normalizing Flow
approaches.problem: We want exact probability and sampling, but flexible generators usually hide the probability of each output.
approaches.how_it_works: Define an invertible neural map between simple noise z and data x. For sampling, draw z from a known base distribution and run the map forward. For likelihood, invert the data point back to z and add the log probability of z to the log determinant of the inverse Jacobian, which accounts for local volume change.
approaches.why_it_matters: It gives a rare combination: generated samples and exact likelihood from the same model.
approaches.failure_mode: Every layer must be invertible and have a tractable volume term, which limits architecture choices.

approaches.name: Coupling Layers
approaches.problem: A fully general invertible neural network can make the volume term too costly to compute.
approaches.how_it_works: Split the vector into two parts. Keep one part unchanged and use it to compute scale and shift values for the other part. This makes the inverse easy because the unchanged part is still available, and it makes the determinant cheap because the Jacobian has a triangular structure. Stack layers with permutations to mix dimensions over time.
approaches.why_it_matters: This makes deep invertible models practical instead of only mathematically possible.
approaches.failure_mode: The split structure can reduce mixing unless many layers and permutations are stacked carefully.

approaches.name: Variational Autoencoder
approaches.problem: Data may be explained by hidden causes, but those causes are not observed.
approaches.how_it_works: Train an encoder q(z|x) to produce a distribution over hidden codes and a decoder p(x|z) to reconstruct or generate observations from those codes. Optimize a lower bound with two forces: reconstruction rewards codes that explain the input, while KL regularization keeps the code distribution close to a simple prior so random sampling works.
approaches.why_it_matters: It gives a trainable way to learn compressed hidden factors while keeping generation possible.
approaches.failure_mode: The decoder can ignore the code, or the prior pressure can make the code too weak.

approaches.name: Reparameterized Sampling
approaches.problem: Sampling a hidden code blocks ordinary gradient training if handled naively.
approaches.how_it_works: Instead of sampling z directly from the encoder distribution in a way that blocks gradients, express the sample as z = mu(x) + sigma(x) * epsilon, where epsilon is fixed external noise from a standard Gaussian. The random part is separated from the learned mean and scale, so backpropagation can update the encoder parameters.
approaches.why_it_matters: This makes latent-variable models trainable with standard neural-network optimization.
approaches.failure_mode: The gradient estimator works only for suitable continuous distributions and can still be noisy or poorly balanced.

approaches.name: Adversarial Training
approaches.problem: Some generators can make samples without giving a usable likelihood to optimize.
approaches.how_it_works: Alternate two updates. First train the discriminator to output high scores for real data and low scores for generated samples. Then freeze or reuse that discriminator signal to update the generator so its samples receive high realness scores. The generator never sees a target image for each noise input; it only follows gradients from the learned judge.
approaches.why_it_matters: It supplies a learned realism signal and can produce sharp samples without pixel-wise averaging.
approaches.failure_mode: The target changes while training, so learning can oscillate, collapse, or stop giving useful gradients.

approaches.name: Discriminator As Learned Loss
approaches.problem: Hand-written losses often reward blurry averages rather than realistic samples.
approaches.how_it_works: Use the discriminator as an adaptive loss function. Instead of measuring pixel distance, the loss asks which features make generated samples distinguishable from real samples. As the discriminator improves, it changes the pressure on the generator, pushing it away from current artifacts and toward statistics that real data shares.
approaches.why_it_matters: The loss adapts to the data instead of measuring only fixed pixel distance.
approaches.failure_mode: The discriminator may focus on superficial clues and give feedback that does not match the desired notion of quality.

approaches.name: Denoising Diffusion
approaches.problem: Making a whole complex sample in one step is difficult and unstable.
approaches.how_it_works: Create supervised pairs by adding known Gaussian noise to clean data at a sampled timestep. Train a network conditioned on the noisy input and timestep to predict the added noise, clean data, or velocity. At sampling time, start from Gaussian noise and repeatedly apply the learned reverse update to move toward clean data.
approaches.why_it_matters: Generation becomes a chain of small repair problems, which is easier to train than a one-shot generator.
approaches.failure_mode: Sampling can be slow because many reverse steps may be needed for high quality.

approaches.name: Guided Sampling
approaches.problem: A generator must often obey a condition such as a class, text prompt, or desired property.
approaches.how_it_works: During denoising, combine the normal data direction with a condition direction. In classifier-free guidance, run the same model with and without the condition, subtract the unconditional prediction from the conditional prediction, and scale that difference before updating the sample. The scale controls prompt or condition strength against diversity.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns an unconditional generator into a controlled generator without changing the whole training setup.
approaches.failure_mode: Too much guidance can reduce diversity or create samples that satisfy the condition in brittle ways.

approaches.name: Contrastive Learning
approaches.problem: A model needs useful features without class labels.
approaches.how_it_works: Generate two augmented views of the same example and encode both into vectors. Pull their vectors close because they share identity, while pushing vectors from other examples away. A temperature-scaled softmax loss such as InfoNCE turns similarity scores into a classification problem: identify the matching view among many distractors.
approaches.why_it_matters: It teaches invariances, such as object identity surviving crop or color changes, from raw data.
approaches.failure_mode: Bad augmentations can erase the very information the representation needs to keep.

approaches.name: Masked Prediction
approaches.problem: The model needs a self-made task that forces it to understand context.
approaches.how_it_works: Corrupt the input by replacing selected words, patches, or regions with mask tokens or noise. Feed the visible parts through the model and train it to reconstruct the hidden content. The mask pattern controls the difficulty: too little masking allows local shortcuts; too much masking removes the context needed to infer the answer.
approaches.why_it_matters: This creates a dense training signal for text, images, and other structured data without labels.
approaches.failure_mode: The model may learn local fill-in tricks instead of broader meaning if the mask task is too easy.

approaches.name: Next-Token Pretraining
approaches.problem: Language has no single label, but every text position supplies a next-piece prediction target.
approaches.how_it_works: Tokenize text and train the transformer to predict token t+1 from tokens up to t. Each position supplies a target, so one document gives many losses. The model reduces loss by learning syntax, facts, discourse patterns, code structure, and common solution shapes, then generation repeats the same prediction loop autoregressively.
approaches.why_it_matters: This simple objective teaches syntax, facts, style, code patterns, and some reasoning habits at scale.
approaches.failure_mode: A good next-token predictor can still produce false, unsafe, or unhelpful answers.

approaches.name: Transformer Context Mixing
approaches.problem: Each word or token must use information from far-away tokens, not only nearby ones.
approaches.how_it_works: Represent tokens as vectors, add position information, and use masked self-attention so each token can gather information from allowed previous tokens. Stacked transformer blocks repeatedly mix context and transform each token vector. Caching key and value states during generation avoids recomputing the whole prefix every time.
approaches.why_it_matters: It gives language models a scalable way to use long context while training on many positions in parallel.
approaches.failure_mode: Cost grows with context length, and the model may still miss facts that require exact retrieval or calculation.

approaches.name: Latent Video Generation
approaches.problem: Raw video is expensive because it has space, time, motion, and many redundant pixels.
approaches.how_it_works: Compress video frames or clips into latent tokens with an encoder, then train the generative model in that smaller space. The model learns spatial detail and temporal change over latent video rather than raw pixels. A decoder converts generated latents back into frames after the motion and scene structure have been produced.
approaches.why_it_matters: It makes video generation cheaper and lets the model spend capacity on motion and scene change instead of every pixel.
approaches.failure_mode: Compression can lose fine details, and small temporal errors can accumulate across frames.

approaches.name: Temporal Consistency Modeling
approaches.problem: A generated video can have good individual frames but bad motion or changing object identity.
approaches.how_it_works: Give the model mechanisms that connect frames: temporal position embeddings, 3D convolutions, attention across space-time tokens, conditioning on previous frames, or motion controls. These links let later frames reuse earlier object identity, layout, and motion state instead of inventing each frame independently.
approaches.why_it_matters: Video quality depends on continuity, not just frame-level realism.
approaches.failure_mode: Long actions, occlusion, and camera motion can still break object identity or physical consistency.

approaches.name: Pseudo-Labeling
approaches.problem: There are many unlabeled examples and only a small labeled set.
approaches.how_it_works: Train an initial model on the labeled set, run it on unlabeled examples, and keep high-confidence predictions as temporary labels. Train again using both real labels and pseudo-labels, often with confidence thresholds and augmentations. The method relies on the model being right often enough that extra practice helps more than it reinforces mistakes.
approaches.why_it_matters: It converts unlabeled data into extra practice when manual labels are scarce.
approaches.failure_mode: Wrong confident guesses can reinforce the model's own mistakes.

approaches.name: Distribution Alignment
approaches.problem: The labeled set and unlabeled set may have different class balance or feature statistics.
approaches.how_it_works: Estimate the model’s average predicted class distribution on unlabeled data and compare it with a desired prior or labeled-data distribution. Rescale or adjust predictions so the aggregate matches that target before using them in the loss. This can prevent class collapse, but only if the target distribution is a reasonable assumption.
approaches.why_it_matters: It prevents the model from treating unlabeled data as if it came from a different problem.
approaches.failure_mode: If the assumed distribution is wrong, alignment can force the model toward false labels.

approaches.name: Constraint-Guided Scientific Generation
approaches.problem: Scientific objects such as proteins or molecules must obey structure, chemistry, and function constraints.
approaches.how_it_works: Represent the scientific object in a domain-aware form, such as sequence, graph, or 3D coordinates, and condition generation on known constraints like structure, chemistry, target binding, or physical feasibility. After sampling, check candidates with validators, simulators, property predictors, or experiments because data likelihood alone does not prove real-world validity.
approaches.why_it_matters: It moves generative modeling from making natural-looking samples to proposing objects that can be tested in the real world.
approaches.failure_mode: A model can exploit dataset patterns while violating hidden physical or experimental constraints.

approaches.name: Property-Conditioned Design
approaches.problem: Scientists often want a new object with a target property, not just a random realistic object.
approaches.how_it_works: Add the desired property as an input to the generator, score candidate samples for that property, and search or sample in regions that satisfy it. The property may be a label, scalar measurement, structure, or learned predictor output. Good design keeps the sample plausible while moving it toward the target measurement.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns generation into design, where the output is judged by usefulness rather than visual realism.
approaches.failure_mode: The requested property may be outside the training data range, so the model's confidence can be misleading.

approaches.name: Neural Radiance Field
approaches.problem: A set of photos shows a scene from some views, but we want to render new views.
approaches.how_it_works: Learn a continuous function that maps a 3D coordinate and viewing direction to density and color. For each training pixel, cast a ray through the scene, sample points along it, query the neural field, and render a predicted pixel. The loss between rendered and observed pixels trains the hidden 3D scene representation.
approaches.why_it_matters: It represents a 3D scene without an explicit mesh and can synthesize realistic novel views.
approaches.failure_mode: Training and rendering can be slow, and wrong camera poses or sparse views can create artifacts.

approaches.name: Volume Rendering
approaches.problem: A camera ray passes through empty space, surfaces, and transparent regions before reaching a pixel color.
approaches.how_it_works: Approximate the light collected by a camera ray. Sample points along the ray, compute each point’s density and color, turn densities into weights that say how much each point contributes before the ray is blocked, and sum weighted colors. This rendering equation connects image supervision to the learned 3D field.
approaches.why_it_matters: It connects the learned 3D field to ordinary image supervision from photos.
approaches.failure_mode: Poor sampling or ambiguous geometry can produce floaters, blurred surfaces, or wrong depth.

approaches.name: Contrastive Multimodal Alignment
approaches.problem: Images, text, audio, and other signals use different forms but can refer to the same thing.
approaches.how_it_works: Encode paired items from different modalities, such as an image and caption, into vectors. Increase similarity for true pairs and decrease similarity for mismatched pairs within the batch. The shared space then supports retrieval, zero-shot classification, and conditioning because related meanings are placed near each other across modalities.
approaches.why_it_matters: It lets one mode retrieve, guide, or explain another, such as text searching images or text steering generation.
approaches.failure_mode: The shared space can capture dataset bias or shallow correlations instead of grounded meaning.

approaches.name: Cross-Attention Conditioning
approaches.problem: A generator needs to use information from another mode while producing its own output.
approaches.how_it_works: Keep generated features as queries and conditioning features as keys and values, or combine both streams in a joint attention layer. At each update, the generator can pull information from text, image, audio, or other context. This creates a direct route for the condition to influence specific generated parts.
approaches.why_it_matters: It gives the generator a direct path to use outside instructions or context during generation.
approaches.failure_mode: The model can ignore the condition, overfit to it, or bind the wrong words to the wrong visual parts.

approaches.name: Data And Model Parallel Training
approaches.problem: Modern models and datasets are too large for one device to train alone.
approaches.how_it_works: Split the work according to the bottleneck. Data parallelism copies the model on each device and averages gradients across batch shards. Model parallelism splits layers or parameters when the model does not fit on one device. Each split requires synchronization, so the gain depends on communication cost as much as compute cost.
approaches.why_it_matters: It makes large unsupervised and generative models trainable within practical time and memory limits.
approaches.failure_mode: Communication can dominate compute, and a poor split can waste hardware.

approaches.name: Pipeline And Tensor Parallelism
approaches.problem: Even one forward pass may not fit or run efficiently on a single accelerator.
approaches.how_it_works: Pipeline parallelism assigns different layer groups to different devices and feeds microbatches through them like an assembly line. Tensor parallelism splits large matrix multiplications across devices and combines partial results. Both methods reduce memory pressure, but they introduce bubbles, synchronization points, and numerical-equivalence checks.
approaches.why_it_matters: These methods attack memory and speed bottlenecks inside very large models.
approaches.failure_mode: Bubbles, synchronization cost, and uneven layer sizes can leave devices idle.
